html:
SMTO-GWT-0031 — SMTO lost track of whether a file copy step finished

GUID: b87ea846-b45c-4b55-ab5e-4269512685dd
Slug: gateway-transfer-receipt-lost
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO lost contact with a computer in the middle of copying a file, so it can't tell whether that step happened. The destination file may already be partly or fully changed. SMTO did not try again on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for both computers in the copy. Both should show Connected. SMTO and you need both computers reachable to see what the interrupted copy left behind.
  2. On the receiving computer, check whether the destination file exists, its size and when it last changed. The lost step may already have written or replaced that file.
  3. Only if the file is missing or clearly incomplete, ask SMTO in a new message to copy it again. Repeating a copy that already finished could replace a file that is already correct.

What success looks like

  • The destination file has the expected size and contents, or a new copy finishes and the Task reports it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateways. Don't repeat the copy until you know what is already at the destination.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GatewayClient.transfer_operation obtained no trustworthy transfer receipt (transport failure, undecodable or mismatched response, or other dispatch error), so the remote transfer outcome is unknown; the client did not retry.

What this means

  • The transfer client could not obtain a trustworthy receipt because of a transport, response-decoding or other unclassified dispatch failure. It does not retry the transfer action automatically. A missing transfer receipt cannot prove that no mutation occurred; retain original ownership and do not replay an uncertain commit.

Why this can happen

  • The transfer client could not obtain a trustworthy receipt because of a transport, response-decoding or other unclassified dispatch failure. It does not retry the transfer action automatically.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original transfer identity and owning Gateway state, especially whether commit was attempted and a destination result exists.

How to fix it

  • Treat the transfer step as possibly applied. Restore Gateway connectivity, then inspect the owning Gateway's transfer state for that transfer ID and the destination path (existence, size, SHA-256) before authorizing any new transfer; never replay a commit whose outcome is unknown.
  • Inspect the owning Gateway transfer state and destination before requesting another transfer. No retry is authorized by this diagnostic.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original transfer and destination are reconciled before authorizing any replacement or repeated mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • A missing transfer receipt cannot prove that no mutation occurred; retain original ownership and do not replay an uncertain commit.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
